caption:
550 kids tested cream, lotion, gel and ointment. Which worked best?

None of them won. In one UK trial, children with eczema were randomly given one of the four for 16 weeks, and eczema scores came out about the same in every group.

What differed was satisfaction. Parents rated gels and lotions highest, creams in the middle, and ointments lowest (378 families answered).

What this doesn't mean: that it's proven for adult faces. The trial was in children aged 6 months to 12 years with eczema, using the study's own products.

Save this for the next time you're stuck in the moisturizer aisle.

General education only. Eczema needs to be diagnosed and treated in person.

Sources: Ridd et al., Health Technol Assess 2023 (doi:10.3310/GZQW6681). Allen et al., Clin Exp Dermatol 2024 (doi:10.1093/ced/llad452).
